subject: English
passage: Kahlo must suffer by her originality. Invent that which is new, even if it be made of clay from your own soil, and there's none to know what you have done. It is because there's no name. This is the cause of Kahlo's lack of recognition. She was Mexican. She was the astounding, inconceivable flowering of her homeland. Gape at her they did, and she at them in amazement. Afterward with mutual hatred, she in disgust, they in mistrust. It is only that which is under your nose that seems most difficult to see.
prompt: What does the text most strongly suggest about Kahlo's work and Mexican viewers?

choices.A: Kahlo's work was so innovative that there was not even terminology to describe it, which led Mexican viewers to regard both the work and Kahlo herself as strange but quintessentially Mexican.
choices.B: Kahlo's work had few fans among Mexican viewers because it tended to present a negative image of Mexican life and institutions.
choices.C: Mexican viewers largely ignored Kahlo's work because its tone and subject matter were out of keeping with mainstream art.
choices.D: Mexican viewers failed to appreciate Kahlo's work because of its novelty and the fact that it reflected aspects of the Mexican character too ingrained in those viewers for them to comprehend.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it captures the text's central paradox about why Kahlo lacked recognition. The text establishes her radical originality ('Invent that which is new... there's no name'), describes her as 'the astounding, inconceivable flowering of her homeland,' and explains that viewers couldn't appreciate her work despite—or rather because of—its deeply Mexican character. The metaphor 'It is only that which is under your nose that seems most difficult to see' indicates that her work reflected Mexican identity so fundamentally that viewers couldn't perceive what was too familiar to them.
